newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba SC shares gain on first trading day.
newsitem.headline: Ciba SC shares gain on first trading day.

text.p: The stock of Swiss speciality chemical company Ciba Speciality Holding Inc. powered higher on its first day of trading on Thursday, crowning one of Europe's biggest spin-offs with solid gains against a generally weaker Swiss stock market.
Shares of Ciba SC, being spun off from pharmaceuticals giant Novartis, closed at 116.50 Swiss francs ($79.25), comfortably above the 110-franc ($74.83), issue price set for its global stock offering.
Opening at 112.75 francs ($76.70), they dipped briefly, then surged to 118 ($80.27), before meeting profit-taking in an otherwise bearish market.

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion francs ($4.6 billion) from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.
The issue price valued the company at around 7.93 billion Swiss francs ($5.4 billion), reflecting surprisingly strong demand.
